title: Tess — queue heuristics & ops checklist
body:
Quick context:
- This is a personal ops scratchpad for the Tess shift (afternoon->evening). Focus is on queue prioritization heuristics, small quick fixes to reduce tail latency, and reminders for capacity adjustments for the next 12 hours.

Top priorities (today):
1) Stop-gap: lower GPU reclaim aggressiveness for pool 's-rt-12' (we hit 2 preempts in last hour causing p95 blips).
2) Validate warm-pool health for frequent API keys (billing buckets A/B).
3) Run a rolling restart of the model-sidecar on nodepool 'infer-eu-1' if memory leak reproduces after 30m.

Heuristics notes (working rules of thumb):
- Small chat/low-token requests (<= 128 tokens) should be favored for latency SLO. If queue depth > 50, route heavy batch jobs to dedicated-backfill pools.
- If a key has >10 repeated prefix cache hits in 5m, keep that key pinned in warm-cache for another 15m.
- Preemptible reclaim: only kick in when node utilization > 92% for >= 5m and pending queue > 200. Otherwise try to shift non-critical batches to dedicated pool.
- Model-variant fallback: when p95 > 300ms for >3m, automatically fallback to the 8-bit quantized variant; alert after fallback if quality regressions reported.
- Network throttling heuristic: if packet-loss > 0.5% across 3 nodes in same rack within 2m, mark rack degraded and move traffic off until manual check.

Immediate todo (check off as done):
- [ ] Adjust reclaim threshold for s-rt-12 to 95% -> 98% for next 6h and monitor. (cmd below)
- [ ] Patch warm-pool eviction TTL from 10m -> 15m for keys A12 and B07.
- [ ] Post note to #infra-alerts: "Proactive reclaim threshold raised for s-rt-12, monitoring p95". Tag: @Evan
- [ ] Run smoke on canary model after sidecar restart (trace id format: ops-YYYYMMDD-HHMM).

Useful commands / snippets (copy-paste):
- Check pool utilization: gcloud compute instances list --filter=\"labels=pool:s-rt-12\" --format=\"table(name,cpuPlatform,status)\"
- Reclaim threshold update (infractl): infractl pools update s-rt-12 --reclaim-threshold 98 --duration 6h
- Inspect warm-pool heatmap: curl -s \"https://console.internal/heatmap?pool=s-rt-12\" | jq '.top_keys[:10]'
- Rolling restart sidecars in infer-eu-1: kubectl rollout restart daemonset/sidecar -n inference --selector=nodepool=infer-eu-1

Metrics to watch (alerts to create/update):
- p95_latency_api: threshold 300ms (SLO breach if sustained >3m).
- node_preempt_events: alert if >1 per 30m for same pool.
- warm_cache_hit_rate: target > 65% for hot keys; if <50% consider bumping TTL.
- rack_packet_loss: alert above 0.5% sustained for 2m.

Handoff for next shift (what to tell the night ops):
- Reclaim threshold bumped for s-rt-12 until 03/14 02:00 UTC. If p95 rises or backlog grows >300, revert reclaim threshold and escalate to SRE.
- Warm-pool TTL increased temporarily; watch warm_cache_hit_rate dashboard (hotkey: infra>cache>warm).
- If infer-eu-1 restarts happen more than twice, open a bug with runtime team (link to PR in metadata).

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Is there a graceful way to migrate long batch jobs to dedicated pools without manual ticketing? (Follow up with @Priya)
- Confirm whether recent sidecar mem-growth is tied to CUDA 12.3 -> 12.4 regression. Evan to run repro on staging.

Notes to self / quick memos:
- Avoid full-scale redis eviction tonight; do targeted key increases.
- Keep handoff message short: what changed, why, what to watch, and immediate rollback steps.
- If manual rollback needed: infractl pools update s-rt-12 --reclaim-threshold 92 --duration 10m

Raw snippets / logs I saved: (paste here during incident)
- last-preempt-log: preempt_events.log -> grep 's-rt-12' | tail -n 50
- tail of sidecar stderr: ssh infer-eu-1 'sudo journalctl -u sidecar -n 300'

End of shift checklist: confirm checkpoints above, send handoff note in #infra-ops, and set a calendar reminder at +5h to re-evaluate TTL change.
